DESCRIPTION: FIND: In `EvidenceRecord.from_chain_record`, the code assumes the untrusted `record["sealed_body"]` dictionary contains all expected keys (`artifact_type`, `recorded_by`, `timestamp_utc`, etc.). However, `VerificationChain.load_json()` does not validate the contents of `sealed_body` — it only ensures the key `"sealed_body"` exists. If a tampered or malformed chain file is loaded, `body["artifact_type"]` (and others) will raise a `KeyError`, crashing the application during `EvidenceStore` initialization before the chain can be verified.
FOLLOW: `EvidenceStore.__init__` crashes on load for structurally corrupted chains. This prevents users from instantiating the store to call `store.verify()` to detect the tampering gracefully, breaking the intended "load then verify" contract and failing closed in an unhandled manner.
